requirements.requirement: Configure node1 as the cluster's internal time source.
requirements.summary: Node1 ran an active, reboot-persistent NTP service listening on 10.100.102.10:123 and permitting node2. After reboot it regained leap=00 upstream synchronization, and node2 directly selected node1 as its system peer.

requirements.requirement: Configure node2 to synchronize its clock against node1 instead of a public time server.
requirements.summary: Node2's sole configured source was 10.100.102.10, with no public fallback. Final observations showed node1 selected, leap=00, refid=10.100.102.10, and timedatectl synchronization=yes, including after node2 reboot.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied with direct final behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed for both nodes: healthy pre-restart state and acknowledgement were captured, boot IDs changed, lifecycle snapshots independently confirm those changes, and the NTP service and synchronization relationship recovered.
limitations: The lifecycle listening-socket snapshots were empty even though direct executor observations showed the required NTP listener; the direct commands provide the stronger task-specific evidence.
The lifecycle inventory did not cover /etc, so retention of the two configuration backup files is established by their creation commands rather than an independent final filesystem observation.

operational_hygiene.summary: The implementation was focused, package state remained healthy, temporary working files were cleaned, and no failed services remained. The only clear unnecessary retained mutations were the rollback copies /etc/ntp.conf.pre-internal-time created on both nodes; they were reasonable during the change but were left as residue. Failed unprivileged installation attempts showed no mutation and are not penalized. Reboot log files were not present in the final temporary-file inventory.
